_comment: English titles and one-line descriptions for the generated guide pages
(scripts/build_topic_pages.py). The Ministry's own topic strings are
Italian and read as bureaucratic Italian even to an Italian, so they make
poor page titles for an American searching in English.
`title` is the <h1> and the first half of the <title> tag. Write it the way
somebody would SAY the subject, not the way the Ministry files it.
`desc` is the meta description and the line under the entry on the index
page: one sentence, under about 155 characters, saying what the page
covers. Both are learner-facing prose, so the app's writing rules apply:
plain English, complete sentences, no colloquialisms.
Keyed by the markdown file's leading number. The generator fails if a
topic has no entry here, so a new topic cannot ship untitled.

01.title: Italian Information Signs
01.desc: Blue and white signs that tell you where you are and what is ahead: route numbers, place names, services, tunnels and lay-bys.

02.title: Italian Mandatory Signs
02.desc: The blue circles that tell you what you must do: compulsory direction, minimum speed, snow chains, and the lanes reserved for each kind of traffic.

03.title: Italian Warning Signs
03.desc: The red triangles, what each one warns of, how far ahead it stands, and what the law expects you to do when you see one.

04.title: Italian Prohibition Signs
04.desc: The red circles: no entry, no passing, no stopping, no parking, weight and size limits, and exactly how far each prohibition reaches.

05.title: Italian Right-of-Way Signs
05.desc: STOP, give way, the priority road and the signs that end it, and which vehicle goes first when two of these meet.

06.title: Italian Temporary and Roadworks Signs
06.desc: Signs at roadworks, complementary signs, delineators and barriers, and why a temporary sign overrides the permanent one beside it.

07.title: Italian Road Markings
07.desc: Lines painted on the road: centre lines, lane lines, edge lines, arrows, crossings and the markings on obstacles, and which may be crossed.

08.title: Italian Supplementary Sign Panels
08.desc: The small rectangular panels under a sign that say how far, how long, which vehicles and which hours the sign above applies to.

09.title: Safe Following Distance in Italy
09.desc: How much space the law requires behind the vehicle in front, how braking distance grows with speed, and the rules for tunnels and heavy vehicles.

10.title: Passing and Overtaking Rules in Italy
10.desc: When you may pass, which side you pass on, where passing is forbidden outright, and what the vehicle being passed has to do.

11.title: Italian Speed Limits
11.desc: The limits on each kind of road, what lowers them, the separate limits for new drivers and for heavy vehicles, and the penalties for exceeding them.

12.title: Stopping and Parking in Italy
12.desc: The difference between fermata, sosta and arresto, where each is allowed, and the rules for parking on a hill, in a town and on a highway.

13.title: Rules of the Road in Italy
13.desc: Where to position your vehicle, how to change lane and turn, who goes first at an intersection, and what to do for emergency vehicles and processions.

14.title: Using Lights and the Horn in Italy
14.desc: Which lights to use by day, at night, in fog and in a tunnel, when the horn may be sounded, and what each warning light on the dashboard means.

15.title: Italian Traffic Lights and Police Signals
15.desc: What each light and arrow means, the yellow you may cross and the yellow you may not, and the hand signals a traffic officer uses.

16.title: Italian Road and Vehicle Definitions
16.desc: The words the Italian road code defines and the exam depends on: carriageway, lane, shoulder, built-up area, and every class of vehicle.

17.title: Fitness to Drive in Italy
17.desc: Alcohol and drug limits, the effect of fatigue, medicines and illness, the blood alcohol table, and the penalties for driving unfit.

18.title: Accident Prevention and First Aid in Italy
18.desc: Defensive driving, what the law requires at the scene of a crash, how to protect the scene, and the first aid you may and may not give.

19.title: Seat Belts and Child Seats in Italy
19.desc: Who must wear a belt and when, how children are restrained by height and age, airbags, helmets, and the reflective vest and warning triangle.

20.title: Vehicle Parts and Maintenance for Safety
20.desc: Tires, brakes, steering, suspension and lights: what each does, how it fails, and the checks the driver is responsible for.

21.title: Loads, Trailers and Breakdowns in Italy
21.desc: Load limits and overhang, towing a trailer or a broken-down vehicle, what to do when you stop on a highway, and the rules for a caravan.

22.title: Italian Driving Licenses and Documents
22.desc: Every license category and its minimum age, the points system, the papers you must carry, and the restrictions on a new driver.

23.title: Insurance and Liability in Italy
23.desc: Compulsory RCA insurance, what civil, criminal and administrative liability each mean, and the penalties for driving uninsured.

24.title: Fuel Economy and Pollution in Italy
24.desc: Driving to use less fuel, what each pollutant does, the rules on noise and idling, and the restrictions a city may impose on traffic.

25.title: Right of Way at Italian Intersections
25.desc: The intersection diagrams the exam draws, the order the vehicles go in, and the rule that decides each one.
